title: How to Get More Patient Reviews Without Being Pushy
desc: Easy, polite ways to collect more five star reviews and build trust with new patients.
text:
Most patients read reviews before they book. A practice with 150 good reviews will often win over a practice with 10, even when the care is the same. The good news is that asking for reviews can feel natural and polite. This guide shows you how to do it step by step.

## Why reviews matter so much
Reviews do three jobs at once. They build trust before a patient ever walks in, because people believe other patients more than they believe your marketing. They also help you rank higher on Google Maps, since Google looks at how many reviews you have and how fresh they are. Finally, they teach you what you do well and what needs work.

A practice with a 4.8 rating and steady new reviews looks active and safe. A practice with a 4.8 rating and no review for two years looks closed.

## Ask at the right moment
Timing is the secret. The best moment is right after a good visit, when the patient still feels happy and relieved. If you wait a week, they forget. A text or email sent the same day gets far more answers than a request a month later.

Good moments to ask include:
- After a successful treatment or a good follow up
- When a patient says thank you or pays a kind compliment
- After a patient finishes a long treatment plan

## Make it very easy
Every extra step loses reviews. Do not ask patients to search for your name and find the review button. Send a direct link to your Google review page by text or email, so one tap opens the review box on their phone. You can also print a small card with a QR code and give it at check out.

## Use a short, friendly message
Keep the message warm and short. For example: "Thank you for visiting us today. If you had a good experience, would you share a short review? It helps other patients find us." Do not tell people what to write, and do not offer gifts or discounts in return.

## Train your front desk team
Your front desk talks to every patient, so they are your best review team. Teach them one simple sentence to say at check out, show them how the link works, and share the wins. When staff see how reviews help the practice, they ask more often and with more confidence.

## Reply to every review
Replying shows future patients that you care. Thank people who leave a good review, and use their first name. When a review is negative, take a breath before you answer. Say sorry that the visit did not go well, keep the reply short, and invite them to call the office to talk. Never confirm that the person was your patient or share any health detail, because that can break privacy rules.

## Follow the platform rules
Do not buy reviews, do not write fake ones, and do not send review requests only to patients you think will be happy. Google and other sites can remove reviews and even punish your listing for these tricks. Honest and steady always wins.

## Keep a steady pace
Aim for a few new reviews each week instead of a rush once a year. Steady growth looks natural and keeps your rating fresh. Track the number every month so you can see your progress.
